deglaciation.name: Ice-sheet retreat
deglaciation.desc: The Scandinavian ice sheet retreats from Pomerania. The Baltic basin still lies under the ice; the first ice-dammed lakes form at its front.

bil.name: Baltic Ice Lake
bil.desc: A lake dammed by the ice and the Øresund sill about 25 m above the ocean of the time. When the ice uncovers Mount Billingen the level drops by 25–28 m.

yoldia.name: Yoldia Sea
yoldia.desc: Connected to the ocean across central Sweden: first through the Billingen corridor, then the Närke strait. Salt water reaches the basin only around 11,700–11,100 cal BP.

ancylus.name: Ancylus Lake
ancylus.desc: Uplift closes the Swedish straits. The lake drains through the Svea River, later the Dana River through the Danish straits; the southern coast is drowned.

mastogloia.name: Mastogloia Sea
mastogloia.desc: The ocean rises faster than the Danish sills. Salt water advances slowly.

littorina.name: Littorina Sea
littorina.desc: Maximum transgression. Salinity clearly higher than today; the sea floods the southern lowlands while the Gulf of Bothnia emerges.

post-littorina.name: Limnaea and Mya Sea
post-littorina.desc: Shallowing of the Danish straits limits inflows. Salinity falls to the present level: about 7 PSU in the Baltic Proper.

billingen-before.label: Before the Billingen drainage
billingen-before.note: Ice still blocks the Billingen corridor. The lake drains through the Øresund.

billingen-after.label: After the Billingen drainage
billingen-after.note: The duration of the drainage is disputed: “1–2 years” is one estimate, not a consensus.

ancylus-max.label: Ancylus maximum
ancylus-max.note: Literature: level about +10 m above the ocean of the time.

ancylus-regression.label: Ancylus regression threshold
ancylus-regression.note: The outlet shifts from the Svea River to the Dana River.

littorina-onset.label: Onset of the Littorina transgression
littorina-onset.note: The ocean spills over the Darss sill.

littorina-max.label: Littorina maximum
littorina-max.note: Mid-Holocene highstand in the transition zones: 7.5–6.5 ka BP.

glossary: Calibrated years before 1950 (Present = 1950). Radiocarbon dates from the literature are converted with IntCal20; without it late-glacial dates shift by 1,000–1,500 years.
Land pressed down by the ice sheet slowly returns to equilibrium. Near Umeå it still rises about 10 mm a year; on the Polish coast hardly at all.
Global change of ocean level due to the water locked in ice sheets. 20,000 years ago the ocean stood about 120 m lower.
Relative sea level: where the water surface stood relative to the present land at a place. It combines isostasy and eustasy — hence H_paleo = H_now − RSL(t) with no separate eustatic term.
The lowest point between a basin and the ocean. In lake phases the sill, not the ocean, sets the Baltic water level.
Practical salinity unit, roughly grams of salt per kilogram of water. Ocean about 35, the Baltic Proper today about 7.
Heights measured against the sea surface of the time, not the present one. Only in this frame is a lake level (e.g. +25 m) one number for the whole basin.
Minimum and maximum ice extent (DATED-1) shown with the most credible outline.

sources.name: GEBCO_2024 Grid — present-day relief and sea floor
sources.use: Present-day height (H_now) across Europe: a 1/20° grid (dem-europe) and 1/40° in the Baltic window (dem-baltic); source of today's coastline, the shading and the paleo-DEM.
sources.origin: GEBCO Compilation Group (2024), GEBCO 2024 Grid, doi:10.5285/1c44ce99-0a0d-5f4f-e063-7086abc0ea0f. Two GeoTIFF tiles (0–90°N / 90°W–0 and 0–90°N / 0–90°E, ice-surface variant) from the CEDA archive (dap.ceda.ac.uk/bodc/gebco).
sources.licence: Public domain with attribution required (Terms of Use of the GEBCO Grid). Copying, processing and publishing are allowed, including commercially.
sources.note: Processing: block average of 12 × 12 and 6 × 6 cells of 15″, mosaic of the tiles. Lakes (Vänern, Vättern, Ladoga, Onega) only have their water surface in GEBCO, no bottom.

sources.name: Steffen & Kaufmann 2025 — relative sea level (RSL)
sources.use: GIA model: the RSL(t) field at 19 steps 21.4 → 0 ka, earth model sk1. The app computes H_paleo = H_now − RSL(t) (no separate eustatic term) and the transect.
sources.origin: Steffen, H., Kaufmann, G. (2025), data on Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.15481755 — files rsl_SK05_skan_<model>.nc, variable RSL, 1° grid, 10°W–70°E / 45–85°N. Ice model in the data: ANU-ICE (1998).
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 — attribution and an indication of changes required.
sources.note: Changes: one of 8 earth models selected (sk1), stored as int16 with 1 cm resolution, linear interpolation in time and bilinear in space.

sources.name: DATED-1 — Eurasian ice-sheet extent
sources.use: Ice in the frames 20 → 10 ka: the most credible outline (mc) as the extent and as a wall in the water model, the min / max outlines as the uncertainty band.
sources.origin: Hughes, A. L. C. et al. (2016), Boreas 45, 1–45, doi:10.1111/bor.12142; data on PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.848117 (DATED-1_TimeSlices_shp.zip, slices TS10–TS20).
sources.licence: CC BY 3.0 — attribution and an indication of changes required.
sources.note: Changes: reprojected from polar LAEA to WGS84, geometry simplified (0.02° tolerance). Event sections take the nearest DATED-1 slice (Billingen: 12 and 11 ka), no interpolation.

sources.name: Chronology and phase descriptions
sources.use: Boundaries of the seven phases (cal BP), names, descriptions in the phase card, water type, indicative salinity ranges (PSU), indicator species, event sections.
sources.origin: Andrén, T. et al. (2011), The Development of the Baltic Sea Basin During the Last 130 ka, in: Harff et al. (eds.), The Baltic Sea Basin, Springer, doi:10.1007/978-3-642-17220-5_4; additions from Björck (1995) and Kotthoff et al. (2022, IODP M0059).
sources.licence: Scientific facts cited from publications (dates, names, ranges). The texts in the app are our own summary, not a reprint.
sources.note: PSU ranges are phase-wide literature values; salinity per basin will come from the model (C-10). Dates are not yet recalibrated with IntCal20 (C-09).

sources.name: Lake levels from the literature (sill-check)
sources.use: The “Level: literature” row of the phase card: Baltic Ice Lake +25 m, Billingen drainage 25–28 m, Ancylus Lake up to +10 m above the ocean of the time.
sources.origin: Values compiled in the data plan (docs/research/baltic-data-plan.md §2) from Björck (1995) and Andrén et al. (2011).
sources.note: “Level: model” is computed by the app (lowest outlet sill, priority-flood); the comparison with the literature is a prototype of test V-02.

sources.name: Sills and places
sources.use: Positions of the sills (Billingen, Närke, Svea, Darss, Drogden, Great Belt), the cities on the globe and the points of the Umeå → Gdańsk transect.
sources.origin: Geographic coordinates from the data plan (§3.2) and public gazetteers; sill elevations and states will come from catalogue C-05.
sources.note: Only the position for now; open / closed state and threshold elevation are not shown.

sources.name: Software
sources.use: Globe rendering, geometry and the interface.
sources.origin: three.js (MIT), d3-geo (ISC), Angular (MIT), lucide (ISC), Inter typeface (SIL OFL 1.1), KMD design system.
sources.licence: Open-source licences listed with each library.

about: This is a prototype, not a scientific result. Heights are real (GEBCO 2024 and the Steffen & Kaufmann 2025 RSL fields), but the pipeline does not have all its steps yet.
H_paleo = H_now − RSL(t) is computed in the browser, linear in time and bilinear in space — the same as the pipeline (agreement < 5 cm).

Water in the Baltic window is filled from the Skagerrak. When the basin has no connection to the ocean it fills up to its lowest outlet sill (priority-flood, ice acts as a wall) — the phase card compares that level with the literature, like the sill-check test (V-02).
Not yet included: the sill catalogue with elevations and states (C-05), salinity per basin (C-10), the eustatic curve (C-12), ice thickness (C-07) and data west of 0°E.
